items.title: Measuring the Permission Gate: A Stress-Test Evaluation of Claude Code's Auto Mode
items.title_zh: 衡量权限门：对 Claude Code 自动模式的压力测试评估
items.summary: The authors present the first independent evaluation of Claude Code's auto mode on deliberately ambiguous authorization scenarios using AmPermBench, a 128-prompt benchmark covering four DevOps task families and three ambiguity axes. They report an end-to-end false negative rate of 81.0% on this stress-test workload, versus the 17% reported on production traffic, with 36.8% of state-changing actions falling outside the classifier's scope through in-project file edits.

items.title: Representational Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Committees: Measurement and Diversity-Aware Consensus
items.title_zh: 多智能体 LLM 委员会中的表征坍缩：测量与多样性感知共识
items.summary: The study embeds each agent's chain-of-thought rationale and measures pairwise similarity across 100 GSM8K questions with three Qwen2.5-14B agents, finding mean cosine similarity of 0.888 and effective rank of 2.17 out of 3.0, a failure mode termed representational collapse. DALC, a training-free consensus protocol using diversity weights from embedding geometry, reaches 87% on GSM8K versus 84% for self-consistency at 26% lower token cost.

items.title: Your Agent is More Brittle Than You Think: Uncovering Indirect Injection Vulnerabilities in Agentic LLMs
items.title_zh: 你的智能体比你想象的更脆弱：揭示智能体 LLM 的间接注入漏洞
items.summary: The authors evaluate six defense strategies against four indirect prompt-injection attack vectors across nine LLM backbones in dynamic multi-step tool-calling environments, finding that advanced injections bypass nearly all baselines and some surface-level mitigations have counterproductive effects. They propose a representation-engineering circuit breaker that uses hidden states at the tool-input position to intercept unauthorized actions.

items.title: Document-Level Numerical Reasoning across Single and Multiple Tables in Financial Reports
items.title_zh: 财务报告单表与多表场景下的文档级数值推理
items.summary: The authors introduce FinLongDocQA, a dataset for single-table and cross-table numerical reasoning in long-context financial reports, and identify two bottlenecks: annual reports often exceed 129k tokens, and models remain error-prone in multi-step arithmetic even when evidence is located. They propose FinLongDocAgent, a multi-agent multi-round RAG approach that iteratively retrieves evidence, performs intermediate calculations and verifies results.

items.title: Are LLM-Based Retrievers Worth Their Cost? An Empirical Study of Efficiency, Robustness, and Reasoning Overhead
items.title_zh: 基于 LLM 的检索器物有所值吗？效率、鲁棒性与推理开销的实证研究
items.summary: The authors reproduce the BRIGHT reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmark across 12 tasks and 14 retrievers, extending evaluation with cold-start indexing cost, latency distributions, throughput, corpus scaling, robustness to query perturbations and confidence calibration. They find some reasoning-specialized retrievers remain competitive in throughput, while several large LLM-based bi-encoders incur substantial latency for modest gains, and confidence calibration is consistently weak.

items.title: FeynmanBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Diagrammatic Physics Reasoning
items.title_zh: FeynmanBench：多模态 LLM 图示物理推理基准
items.summary: FeynmanBench is a benchmark of more than 2,000 tasks built on Standard Model Feynman diagrams that requires models to recover vertices, propagators, topology, momentum routing and full scattering amplitudes. Across 19 multimodal LLMs, the authors find 70-95% accuracy on local recognition but only 13-17% on topological reconstruction and near zero on full algebraic derivation.

items.title: MMP-Refer: Multimodal Path Retrieval-augmented LLMs For Explainable Recommendation
items.title_zh: MMP-Refer：面向可解释推荐的多模态路径检索增强 LLM
items.summary: MMP-Refer is a framework that uses multimodal retrieval paths with a retrieval-augmented LLM for explainable recommendation, obtaining multimodal embeddings from a sequential recommendation model and using a heuristic search to construct retrieval paths. A trainable lightweight collaborative adapter maps interaction-subgraph encodings into the LLM's semantic space as soft prompts.

items.title: VectifyAI/OpenKB
items.summary: OpenKB is an open-source knowledge base for large language models, written in Python.
